thread:
ash_support: FYI customer j.jones reported a p99 spike starting ~2026-03-17 02:03 UTC after our weekend infra push. Also seeing intermittent 5xx on /v1/generate and billing alert for doubled token counts. Escalating to incidents.
kate_sre: ack. any repro steps or logs from the customer? link? :eyes:
ash_support: pasted their snippet below, says spike correlates with SDK client retries. They hit ~p99 2.1s -> 12.5s. auth failures intermittently 502. Billing showed a burst of retries.
ash_support: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":256}'```
ash_support: customer logs: "request_id=abc123 latency=12.45s status=502 auth_err=invalid_token? attempts=3"
ben_eng: sounds like a degraded host/kernel path + retry amplification. Did we roll any drivers/firmware last night?
ivan_ops: we pushed cuda-driver-14.2.1+gpu-fw-2026-03-16 at 00:30 UTC to eu1-edge nodes (canary then ring). Kernel host updates were also staged on a subset (host-kernel-5.18.23).
kate_sre: that timing matches. Also saw NVMe qdepth climb on eu1-rt-* around 00:35. Could be storage contention causing request tail latency and auth proxy timeouts.
claire_billing: on billing side the doubled tokens look like client retries hitting our rate limiter differently — retries create duplicate charge events before dedupe. We throttled insecure paths at 03:00 which reduced but didn't fully stop the burst.
ash_support: customer included a short transcript: "started at 02:03, retried 3x, got 502 on 2 attempts then succeeded on 3rd"
ben_eng: immediate mitigations: 1) add routing policy to prefer eu2/hostpool for this customer's traffic, 2) enable short circuit fallback to model-compat variant (lower mem) for requests >2s, 3) open rollback for driver canary.
kate_sre: also enable KV cache bypass for affected hosts to avoid long IO on cold miss bursts. We should increase autoscale min replicas for eu1-edge by +20% temporarily.
ivan_ops: adding actionables: rolling back cuda-driver on canary hosts now (iv-rollback-2078901234), isolating nvme-heavy hosts from serving pool, and increasing qdisc writeback tunables.
oncall_bot: Incident created INC-207890-89: "eu1-edge p99 spike after driver & fw push — auth/billing impact" assigned to kate_sre, priority P1.
ben_eng: repro steps for infra team (quick): 1) deploy canary driver 14.2.1 to single eu1 node, 2) run load generator with prefix-sharing to trigger KV cache cold misses, 3) observe nvme qdepth, kernel iowait, and per-token latencies.
ben_eng: sample load command: ```python -m locust -f tests/load_gen.py --host=https://eu1-edge.redwood.ai -u 200 -r 50 --run-time 5m --headers "Authorization: Bearer <token>"```
kate_sre: good. while we bisect, set per-account retry-window dedupe and billing hold for j.jones to prevent billing noise. claire_billing can you hold charges?
claire_billing: placing a temporary billing hold and opening refund ticket for any duplicate charges flagged by support. will follow up in support ticket.
ash_support: notified customer that we're investigating, gave workaround to switch region + asked for full request_id list. they responded with 6 request_ids.
ivan_ops: rolling back driver on 3 canary hosts now, will monitor nvme queuing metrics and tail latencies. ETA 10m.
ben_eng: also capture perf recordings: run perf + eBPF traces during repro to look for nvme syscall backpressure and GPU stalls.
kate_sre: short-term hotfix: 1) pin routing off the updated host pool 2) increase auth proxy timeout to 10s for affected routes 3) disable aggressive client-side retries in gateway. These will reduce amplification.
ash_support: customer accepted region switch for now and will wait for rollback. thanks team. :thumbsup:
ivan_ops: rollback completed on canaries. initial metrics: nvme qdepth down 60%, p99 request latency back near baseline after 6 minutes. auth 502s reduced.
kate_sre: keep monitoring for 1h, then decide on controlled rollout with storage IO tuning and kernel knob adjustments (raise nomerges? tune nr_requests?).
ben_eng: follow-ups: 1) schedule postmortem with timeline & RCA 2) add gating to future driver/firmware rollouts to include NVMe + kernel IO benchmarks under KV-cache-heavy traffic 3) investigate retry dedupe for billing events. assigning owners.
claire_billing: will report refund status and update billing playbook to block duplicate charge creation on rapid retry spikes.
ash_support: closing loop with customer, sending interim RCA when we have it. will link INC ticket to support thread.
kate_sre: adding note: possible root cause = driver/firmware combo causing increased IO stalls on certain nvme HW; that amplified client retries -> auth proxy timeouts -> duplicate billing signals. final RCA pending after eBPF traces.
ash_support: thanks all. I'll add log excerpts to the incident and assign follow-up PRs. :rocket:
